newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish TPSA shares to be floated in 1998 - minister.
newsitem.headline: Polish TPSA shares to be floated in 1998 - minister.

text.p: Poland's telecommunications ministry aims to launch shares of state telecoms firm TPSA SA on the Warsaw and foreign bourses in 1998, preferably at the start of the year, minister Andrzej Zielinski said on Monday.

"We would like to introduce TPSA shares on this country's bourse and abroad in 1998, at the beginning of the year if possible, and all the essential preparations will be made during 1997," Zielinski told a news conference.

"A minority package of shares will be sold simultaneously in the country and abroad," the telecommunications minister said without giving details of what proportion of the shares in Telekomunikacja Polska SA (TPSA) would be sold.
The company's further privatisation steps were flexible, he said, adding: "This means either further public offering or an invitation to a strategic investor."
Zielinski said the TPSA privatisation plan had taken account of analysis by investment banks Schroders and CS First Boston, advising the government, as well as TPSA's Polish advisors.
He had already submitted a letter to the cabinet and assumed the government would examine the plan next month.
Zielinski said privatisation would precede a liberalisation of Poland's telecommunications market in which TPSA currently holds a monopoly on long-distance connections.

Liberalisation of inter-city links would take place after 1999 and of international ones after 2003, while this was being discussed by the Polish government and the World Trade Organisation (WTO), he said.
Under an agreement with the WTO, Poland has to liberalise international connections by 2002.

Poland's official watchdog, the Supreme Auditing Chamber, ruled this month that TPSA had been abusing its position as a virtual monopolist, limiting private firms' access to local markets and keeping long-distance prices high.
A statement released at the conference said one key task would be to bring TPSA's financial standards into line with those in other countries.
